title: Domination of an excellent surface modification by normalized point blowups
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral excellent Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-exc-excellent-ring] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], where excellence means excellence of every affine coordinate ring. Let $f:Y\to S$ be a proper morphism with $Y$ integral, inducing an isomorphism of function fields [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sc-function-field]. There are an integer $n\geq0$, a sequence $S_n\to\cdots\to S_0=S$ of proper morphisms, and an $S$-morphism $S_n\to Y$ factoring the composite $S_n\to S$. Every $S_{j+1}\to S_j$ is the blowup at a reduced closed point followed by normalization in its function field [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-sc-normalization]. The schemes $S_j$ are integral and normal, and these morphisms induce isomorphisms of function fields. No regularity of $S_n$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BBT, resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up, specialized to normal excellent integral S (excellence implies Nagata); its initial normalization is the identity because S is normal. Properness of the arrows is resolve-lemma-Nagata-normalized-blowup.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves] to $f:Y\to S$. It supplies a finite proper normalization $q:Y_0\to Y$ and a proper function-field isomorphism $f_0:Y_0\to S$ with $Y_0$ normal integral excellent Noetherian of dimension $2$. A tower mapping to $Y_0$ maps to the original $Y$ by composition with $q$. The normalization of the normal integral $S$ is $S$ itself: its local rings are already integrally closed in $k(S)$, so the integral-closure construction in [def-sc-normalization] leaves them unchanged. Thus the initial normalization in the source introduces no extra arrow in the required tower.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof first paragraph: normalize the source and identify the normal target with its normalization

proof.text: We prove the assertion for every proper function-field isomorphism $h:Z\to X$ between normal integral excellent Noetherian surfaces by strong induction on the finite integer $r=|B(h)|$, with $B(h)$ as in [lem-per-normal-surface-exceptional-curves]. If $r=0$, that node says $h$ is an isomorphism; use the tower of length zero and its inverse $X\to Z$. For $r>0$, assume the assertion proved for every such morphism with fewer than $r$ contracted curves. The construction in the following steps will reach a new such morphism with fewer than $r$ curves after finitely many normalized point blowups of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof second paragraph: induction on the number of contracted curves and the empty base case

proof.text: Choose $C\in B(h)$, let $x=h(C)$, and put $R=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta_C}$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The exceptional-curve node makes $x$ closed, $R$ a DVR, $A\to R$ an injective local map of domains with common fraction field $K$, and $\kappa(\eta_C)/\kappa(x)$ of transcendence degree one. Choose an element of that residue field transcendental over $\kappa(x)$ and lift it to $u\in R$. Write $u=a/b$ in $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, with $a,b\in A$ nonzero. This uses only the definition of a fraction field after the cited identifications.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof fourth paragraph: choose u in the local ring at the generic point of the exceptional curve (correcting the printed X,C subscript)

proof.text: Write $v:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for the order valuation of the DVR $R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The nonzero residue of $u$ gives $v(u)=0$, so $v(a)=v(b)\geq0$. If $b$ were a unit of $A$, reduction of $a/b$ would belong to $\kappa(x)$, contradicting its transcendence. Thus $b\in\mathfrak m_A$; locality gives $v(b)>0$, hence $v(a)>0$ and $a\in\mathfrak m_A$ too. Set $N=\min(v(a),v(b))>0$. These are just the unit and maximal-ideal tests for a local map to a valuation ring.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof fourth paragraph: positivity of the valuation induction parameter

proof.text: Blow up the reduced closed point $x$ and normalize to obtain $g:X_1\to X$. Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalized-blowup-tower] to the length-one tower over the normal $X$ (its initial normalization is $X$). It says that $X_1$ is a normal integral excellent Noetherian surface and that $g$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense and induces an isomorphism of function fields. Hence $g$ is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. Apply [lem-per-normalized-surface-graph-exceptional-injection] to $(h,g)$, obtaining proper birational $h_1:Z_1\to X_1$, $p_1:Z_1\to Z$ and an injection $B(h_1)\hookrightarrow B(h)$, with $Z_1$ again a normal integral excellent Noetherian surface. If $|B(h_1)|<r$, stop this construction. Otherwise the injection between finite sets of size $r$ is a bijection, so $C$ has exactly one preimage $C_1$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof third paragraph: normalized dominating graph, injection, and reduction to eliminating a selected curve

proof.text: In the persistence case put $x_1=h_1(C_1)$ and $A_1=\mathcal O_{X_1,x_1}$. The graph-injection node says that $x_1$ is closed, lies over $x$, that $\kappa(x_1)/\kappa(x)$ is finite, and that $\mathcal O_{Z_1,\eta_{C_1}}=R$ inside $K$. The local maps $A\to A_1\to R$ commute. Consequently the same residue of $u$ remains transcendental over $\kappa(x_1)$: if it were algebraic over that field, the tower of two algebraic extensions would make it algebraic over $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof last paragraph: persistence of the generic DVR and of the transcendental residue

proof.text: The ideal sheaf of the reduced closed point is finite type: on each Noetherian affine it is an ideal in a Noetherian ring, hence finitely generated. The principalization theorem [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] says that on the ordinary blowup the extended ideal of $x$ is generated locally by a non-zero-divisor. At the image of $x_1$ choose such a generator and call its image in $A_1$ $d$. The ideal of $x$ is nonzero because the integral $X$ has dimension $2$, so the ordinary blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_x X$ is integral [lem-per-integral-blowup-projective-geometry] with function field $K$, and $d$, a non-zero-divisor of its local ring, is nonzero there. Normalization is dominant between integral schemes with the same function field, so this nonzero element remains nonzero. Extension of the ideal gives $\mathfrak m_A A_1=dA_1$, and $d\in\mathfrak m_{A_1}$ since $x_1$ lies over $x$. Thus $a=a_1d$ and $b=b_1d$ for some nonzero $a_1,b_1\in A_1$, with $u=a_1/b_1$. No assertion that an arbitrary pullback of a Cartier ideal stays Cartier is needed; here all local rings embed into $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof last paragraph: local equation d for the exceptional ideal and division of a,b

proof.text:
The map $A_1\to R$ is local, so $v(d)>0$. The DVR multiplication rule yields
$$N_1=\min(v(a_1),v(b_1))=N-v(d)<N.$$
The argument of Step 4, now over $A_1$ and using the transcendental residue over $\kappa(x_1)$, shows $a_1,b_1\in\mathfrak m_{A_1}$ and $N_1>0$. Explicitly, a unit denominator would give a residue in $\kappa(x_1)$; equality of the two valuations and locality then force both valuations positive. This is elementary arithmetic in the same DVR, whose valuation has not changed.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof final displayed order equality: strict decrease if the curve persists

proof.text: Repeat Steps 5--8 with $(X_i,Z_i,h_i,C_i,a_i,b_i)$ in place of $(X,Z,h,C,a,b)$ as long as $|B(h_i)|=r$. Inductively, both schemes remain normal integral excellent Noetherian surfaces, the maps to the previous $Z_i$ compose to $Z$, the injections identify the unique continuing curve with $C$, and its generic DVR is always $R$. The contraction points have successive finite residue extensions, and $N_i>0$ decreases by at least one at every persistence step. Thus persistence for $N$ steps would give $0<N_N\leq0$, a contradiction. At some finite stage $j\geq1$ we therefore have $|B(h_j)|<r$. The only maps appended to the base tower were normalized blowups at reduced closed points; the graph maps were used solely for the auxiliary sources.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof fourth and last paragraphs: descending induction on the positive integer order, with the tower invariant explicit

proof.text: Apply the outer strong induction hypothesis to $h_j:Z_j\to X_j$. It gives a finite normalized point-blowup tower $T\to\cdots\to X_j$ and an $X_j$-map $T\to Z_j$. Concatenate it with $X_j\to\cdots\to X$ and compose $T\to Z_j\to Z$. This proves the induction step on $r$. Applying the result to $f_0:Y_0\to S$ of Step 1 and composing with $Y_0\to Y$ gives the requested $S$-map. All base-tower schemes are integral and normal, and all base arrows are proper and preserve function fields by Step 5 at each stage. The case where $f_0$ is already an isomorphism uses $n=0$. The argument never asserts that an endpoint is regular.

source.place: Tag 0BBT (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-normalized-blowing-up), proof completion: outer induction, concatenation, and composition back to the original Y
